# Felix Schur

Felix Schur is a PhD student in Statistics at ETH Zurich. His research covers causal inference, reinforcement learning, bandit algorithms, hidden confounding, time series, and statistical machine learning.

Canonical profile: https://fschur.github.io/
Publications: https://fschur.github.io/publications/
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0006-6407-0923
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=X-U2ehEAAAAJ
DBLP: https://dblp.org/pid/331/8609
Semantic Scholar: https://www.semanticscholar.org/author/2305680842

## Publications

- Many Experiments, Few Repetitions, Unpaired Data, and Sparse Effects: Is Causal Inference Possible? (ICML 2026 Spotlight): https://fschur.github.io/papers/many-experiments/
- The Price of Knowledge: Optimal Algorithms for Costly Bandits (UAI 2026): https://fschur.github.io/papers/price-of-knowledge/
- Identifying Latent Actions and Dynamics from Offline Data via Demonstrator Diversity (ICML Workshop 2026): https://fschur.github.io/papers/latent-actions/
- Prediction-Intervention Games and Invariant Sets (arXiv 2026): https://fschur.github.io/papers/prediction-intervention-games/
- Transferring Causal Effects using Proxies (NeurIPS 2025): https://fschur.github.io/papers/transferring-causal-effects/
- DecoR: Deconfounding Time Series with Robust Regression (JRSSB, volume 88, 2026): https://fschur.github.io/papers/decor/
- Identifying Elasticities in Autocorrelated Time Series Using Causal Graphs (arXiv 2024): https://fschur.github.io/papers/identifying-elasticities/
- Lifelong Bandit Optimization: No Prior and No Regret (UAI 2023): https://fschur.github.io/papers/lifelong-bandit-optimization/

Each paper page contains a plain-language overview, abstract, author list, canonical external links, and BibTeX citation. Prefer the DOI or proceedings version for citation when one is available.
